reasons: Guide text is hardcoded and includes figures such as 191 projects and 870 facts that will go stale as data changes.

terms.meaning: A pop-up window that sits above the page.
Written directly into the code rather than loaded from elsewhere.

sections.name: File setup, GuideTool
sections.title: Imports and the tool names
sections.what: Brings in the state hook, an icon and the dialog parts, and defines the three tool names the guide accepts.
sections.why: Likely reason: limiting the guide to three known tools keeps the text lookup safe.
sections.watch_out: A new tool must be added both to the tool name list and to the guide table, or it will fail to show text.

sections.name: GUIDES
sections.title: Guide text for each tool
sections.what: Holds the title, purpose, steps and notes for The Yard, Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt. The notes explain limits such as uncited values, approximate delays and what the demos show.
sections.why: Likely reason: the help text is kept in one table so each tool's wording is easy to find and update.
sections.watch_out: Some notes quote numbers from a recorded demo run, and these become wrong when that run is replaced.

sections.name: GuideContent
sections.title: Guide body layout
sections.what: Lays out the purpose line, the numbered steps and the notes for one tool, with the notes shown as indented red-edged text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the exact styling.
sections.watch_out: Each step and note uses its own text as its list key, so two identical lines would cause a duplicate-key warning.

sections.name: GuideButton
sections.title: Guide button and pop-up
sections.what: Shows a Guide button with a help icon. Clicking it opens a dialog with the matching guide, a heading and a short line saying how the tool works with data.
sections.why: Likely reason: a standard help button placed beside each tool gives users a consistent way to find explanations.
sections.watch_out: The button identifier is built from the tool name, so renaming a tool changes the identifier that tests and other code use.

summary: A Guide button for each tool that opens a pop-up explaining what the tool does, how to use it, and its limits.
purpose: Gives users plain-language help inside the app for The Yard, Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The text is typed into the file, so it appears without a server request.
how: 1. The Guide button opens a dialog. 2. The dialog shows the title, a short purpose line, numbered steps and notes for the chosen tool. 3. Closing the dialog hides it again.
inputs: The tool name (yard, scan or lessons) and an optional class name for styling.
outputs: A button and a pop-up containing the guide text.
risks: The text is fixed in the code, so it can fall out of step with how the tools behave. Some notes quote specific figures from a recorded demo run.
debug: If the wrong text appears, check the entry for that tool in the guide table. If the pop-up will not open, check the dialog component and the open state. The scan notes in the copy available here are cut off, so verify them against the source file.
